technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Framework 6.0+ and Java 17+ as the baseline for all module development.
Leverage existing Spring Integration extensions for AWS, WebSocket, Cassandra, and SOLR to minimize custom code.

Implement the error channel using Spring Integration's standard messaging and error handling capabilities, defining a custom exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException).
For the HAWQ sink, utilize Apache Avro and Parquet libraries to format data before writing via PXF extensions.
Design all source and sink modules as independent, configurable components that can be dynamically added or removed.
assumptions: The base application framework, build pipeline, and deployment infrastructure are already established.
Access to AWS (S3, SES), Cassandra, SOLR, and HAWQ/PXF test environments is readily available.
The data partition strategy state preservation feature (U8) is already implemented in the codebase, and only testing effort is needed.
Development includes unit testing, but end-to-end integration testing is a separate activity.
All estimates are in work-hours and represent the effort of a single developer.

activities.activity_description: Overall design of the new source and sink modules, integration points, and the error channel architecture.
Implement the WebSocket source module to ingest browser-based events and activities (U1).
Implement the AWS source module to ingest data from Amazon S3 and use Simple Email Service (SES) (U2).
Implement the Cassandra sink module to write high volumes of variable data (U3).
Implement the AWS sink module to write data directly into S3 (U4).
Implement the HAWQ sink module to write data via PXF extensions using Avro/Parquet formats (U5).
Implement the SOLR sink module for full-text indexing and search (U6).
Implement the configurable error channel, custom exception hierarchy, and error staging/routing logic (U7).
Perform testing for the data partition strategy state preservation when adding/deleting modules (U8).
Conduct end-to-end integration testing of all new modules and error handling, and update documentation.
